abstract: One of the underlying mechanisms of sperm cell DNA damage is oxidative stress. People with overweight or obese tend to have high oxidative stress in plasma and urine. Due to this reason, this study was aimed to investigate the association between body mass index and DNA Fragmentation Index in male partners from infertile couples at Halim Fertility Center’s Stella Maris Mother’s and Children’s Hospital. This study was an observational study with a cross-sectional design among 40 male partners from infertile couples at Halim Fertility Center’s Stella Maris Mother’s and Children’s Hospital selected by convenience sampling. This study showed a positive, very strong correlation between Body Mass Index and DNA Fragmentation index (P-value < 0.05; R Squared = 0.998). Half of the male couples as samples had a body mass index value between 19.50 to 28.33 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and DNA fragmentation index of 2.00 to 11.50%, while the remaining half showed a body mass index value of greater than 28.33 to 34.72 kg/m2 and DNA fragmentation index between greater than 11.5 to 44.00%. Thus, it can be concluded that body mass index affects the DNA Fragmentation Index value in the infertile couple.

articleTitle: Anti-Dyslipidemia Activity from Lemon Pepper in PTU and High Fat Diet Induced Rats
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Riskesdas in 2013 showed that 35.9% of the Indonesian population aged higher than 15 years had abnormal cholesterol levels. Lemon pepper has various pharmacological benefits. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effectiveness of lemon pepper methanol extract as anti-dyslipidemia. This study is an experimental study using 24 rats divided into 6 different groups, including: normal (no intervention), control (Na CMC 0.5%), standard (simvastatin), Lemon Pepper Methanol Extract I (300 mg/kgBW), II (600 mg/kgBW), and III (1200 mg/kgBW). All groups, except the normal group, were given a high-fat diet (15 g/kg animal fat; 10 g/kg poultry egg yolk) and PTU (12.5 mg/day). The results showed that the highest dose of lemon pepper methanol extracts significantly reduced total cholesterol (151.75 ± 0.96 mg/dl), triglycerides (166.50 (162-179) mg/dl), and LDL cholesterol (68.50 ± 1.29 mg/dl) levels and significantly increased HDL levels (61.00 (60-100) mg/dl) compared to the control group. In addition, the lemon pepper methanol extract significantly reduced the levels of SGOT (P value same 0.029) and SGPT (P value smaller than 0.05) compared to the control group. Hence, it can be said that the methanol extract of lemon pepper has an anti-dyslipidemic effect and can prevent NAFLD.

articleTitle: Antibiofilm Activity of Parabiotic Reuterin on Acrylic Resin Plates
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Denture stomatitis is the most common debilitating problem among denture users worldwide. An alternative treatment could be natural probiotics. Probiotic Lactobacillus reuteri produces an antimicrobial substance called reuterin. The aim of this study is to evaluate effectiveness of parabiotic reuterin towards Candida albicans and Staphylococcus aureus biofilms on acrylic resin plates. The minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of reuterin towards C. albicans and S. aureus were evaluated. Thereafter, standard preventive and therapeutic assays were performed on biofilms grown on acrylic denture plates. The effect of reuterin on biofilms was quantified with crystal violet staining, colony counting, and qPCR. The experimental data were analyzed by appropriate statistical tests. The MICs of reuterin towards S. aureus and C. albicans were 100µg/mL and 25µg/mL, respectively (p<0.05). Interestingly, reuterin exhibited antibiofilm activity against S. aureus and C. albicans at 100 µg/mL and eradicated the biofilms by 24 h incubation (p<0.05). Moreover, reuterin was effective against monospecies and mixed-species biofilms on acrylic plates. This pilot study showed that reuterin has an antibiofilm activity against C.albicans and S.aureus biofilms by reducing biofilms’ number as much as 83% and 94.5 % respectively, in the denture acrylic plate model Hence, result will provide a basis for developing reuterin as a probiotic-based natural solution for denture stomatitis in the future.

articleTitle: Antioxidant Activity of Green Tea Extract and Myricetin
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Free radicals are the major cause of oxidative stress, which can lead to inflammatory diseases, ischemic diseases, hemochromatosis, emphysema, and other illnesses. Antioxidant intake is essential for keeping the body's oxidative processes in balance. Green tea containt a natural antioxidant that is commonly consumed and readily available. Myricetin is a pure component of green tea. This study aims was to determine the antioxidant activity of green tea extract (GTE) compared with myricetin (MYR). Antioxidant activity properties were determined by 2,2-diphenyl-1 picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), 2,2 ′ -Azinobis(3-Ethylbenzthiazoline-6-Sulfonate) (ABTS), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), NO scavenging, and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP). The analysis results showed that the IC50 of GTE (24.00 µg/mL) was higher than MYR (4.68 µg/mL) in DPPH scavenging activity. The highest concentration of FRAP activity of GTE and MYR were 595.78±19.35 and 530.67±10.97 μM Fe (II)/µg. GTE also had a higher IC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> value for ABTS reducing activity than MYR, at 25.16 µg/mL versus 16.78 µg/mL. According to H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> scavenging activity, MYR has higher antioxidant activity (133.32 µg/mL) than GTE (137.31 µg/mL). Meanwhile, the NO scavenging assay results show that MYR (19.70 µg/mL) has a higher IC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> value than GTE (7.10 µg/mL). In conclusion, GTE has potential antioxidant activity like its particular compound, MYR.

articleTitle: The Hepatoprotective Effect of White Turmeric Ethanol Extract on Cyclophosphamide-Induced Male Wistar Rats
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Antioxidants are essential substances that can prevent damage caused by oxidative stress to the liver. Alternative solutions for the reduction of the negative effects of free radicals on the liver might be white turmeric. The aim of this study was to evaluate (using three indicators: Serum Glutamic Oxalocaetic Transaminase and Serum Glutamic Pyruvic Transaminase enzymes, peripheral blood, and hepatic cell histology) the level of the protective impact of white turmeric on the rat’s liver. In this study 30 rats which were divided into 6 groups normal group (without treatment), a negative control group (Na-CMC 0.5%), a positive control group (Catechins), and 3 experimental groups given the ethanol extract white turmeric rhizome with various doses. All rats in each groups were given 150 mg/kg body weight of cyclophosphamide solution on days 11 to 15 of the trial. The results revealed that the Serum Glutamic Oxalocaetic Transaminase and Serum Glutamic Pyruvic Transaminase levels decreased along with a dosage increase in the group with ethanol extract of white turmeric and an improvement in homeostasis and the histopathology of the liver of the rats. Particularly at a dose of 800 mg / kg body weight, indicated the amount Serum Glutamic Oxalocaetic Transaminase and Serum Glutamic Pyruvic Transaminase that was closest to the value of the normal group.

articleTitle: Phytochemical and Hypoglycemia Effect Test Using Extract of Barangan Banana Peel with OGTT in Male White Rats Induced with Sucrose
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Generally, banana peel extracts are needed to develop numerous antidiabetic drugs due to their antihyperglycemic effects on blood sugar levels. Therefore, this research proposes to discover the hypoglycemic and phytochemical effects of barangan banana peel extract by analyzing the oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT) using white male rats induced with sucrose. The results showed that the phytochemical tests carried out in the experiment produced positive results on all examinations. In OGTT, the difference in blood sugar levels was insignificant from -30 to 0 minutes. However, after 30 minutes, a significant difference in the aquadest group was observed at the dose of 500 and 1000 mg/kg BW, which was similar in the group of rats treated with glibenclamide. Furthermore, the dose of 500 mg/kgBW showed the most significant reduction value (102.80 ± 5.54ab) at the latest minutes of observation, compared to the aquadest (171.80 ± 13.33) and glibenclamide (75.20 ± 6.9a) groups. In conclusion, the research showed that barangan banana peel extract could be used as an antidiabetic drug.

articleTitle: Nephroprotective Effect from Rose Petals (Rosa damascena) Extract Against Cadmium Toxicity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Cadmium, a heavy metal, is commonly used in industries. It could accumulate in various bodily organs, especially in the kidneys. Due to its antioxidative effect, rose (Rosa damascena) petal may serve to protect organs and tissues against free radicals, generated by cadmium deposition. Hence, this study aims to investigate the nephroprotective effect from rose petal extract against cadmium toxicity. This study was experimentally-designed that involved 25 male Wistar rats, divided into five different groups viz. control (Na-CMC), standard (Quercetin), rose petal methanol extract-I (400 mg/kg BW), extract-II (800 mg/kg BW), and extract-III (1.2g/kg BW). All rats received 7 mg/kgBW of cadmium sulfate peroral 30 minutes following quercetin or rose extract administration. After four weeks of treatment, all rats were sacrificed. Blood and kidney tissue were collected for examinations. Based on lab parameter, it showed that 400 to 1.2 g/kgBW of rose extract was able to maintain similar amount of blood ureum with that of the standard group (p value < 0.05), therefore protecting the tubular part of the kidneys from cadmium damage. The extract III groups exhibited most minimal kidney damage, quantified via lowest EGTI score. Thus, rose petal extract has nephroprotective effect against cadmium toxicity.

articleTitle: Anti-Aging Effectiveness of Red Spinach Extract Ointment (Amaranthus Tricolor L.) Against Collagen, Elasticity, Hydration, Sebum, and Pigment Levels in Wistar Rats
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Skin aging is a complex natural phenomenon characterized by a progressive loss of structural integrity and physiological function of the skin. These changes manifest as visible wrinkling and loss of elasticity in the skin. This study aims to assess the anti-aging effectiveness of red spinach extract on increasing levels of collagen, elasticity, hydration, sebum, and pigment in male rats. A total of 25 rats were divided into 5 groups, each of which consisted of 5 white rats; control group (ointment base), red spinach extract ointment group 2.5%, 5%, 7.5%, and 10%. The results of phytochemical examination showed the presence of alkaloids, flavonoids, tannins and glycosides, with the total content of phenols, tannins, and flavonoids from the methanol extract of spinach leaves, respectively 20.22 GAE mg / gram extract, 0.09 QE mg / gram extract, and 20.83 TAE mg / gram extract. Changes in the level of skin hydration before and after treatment showed a significant change (P value less than 0.05) with the highest change found at a concentration of 10%, namely 64.84%. Changes in skin collagen levels before and after treatment showed significant changes (P value less than 0.05) with the highest change found at a concentration of 10%, namely 56.25%. Changes in the level of skin elasticity before and after treatment showed significant changes (P value less than 0.05) with the highest change found at a concentration of 10%, namely 46.30%. Changes in the level of skin pigmentation before and after treatment showed a significant change (P value less than 0.05) with the highest change found at a concentration of 10%, namely 35.97%. The highest percentage of decrease in sebum level among all groups given red spinach methanol extract ointment was indicated by the highest concentration of 10%, which was 40%. From the results of this study, it can be concluded that the red spinach leaf extract ointment has quite good anti-aging activity.

articleTitle: Anti-diabetic Activity of The Rose Petal Methanolic Extract in Alloxan-Diabetic Rats
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Based on the Riskesdas 2013 report, the number of DM people in Indonesia is very high. Recently, the herb is a quietly demanding drug and has a high demand in the market. The rose petal has been investigated for anti-diabetic properties. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the anti-diabetic activity of rose petals methanol extract in alloxan-induced male Wistar rats. This study was an experimental study using 25 Wistar rats. All rats were initially induced by 5% alloxan (150 mg/kg BW). After 48 hours, all rats were grouped into five different groups, viz. control (Na-CMC 0.5%), standard (Metformin), Rose Methanol Extract I (750 mg/kg BW), II (1000 mg/kg BW), and III (1500 mg/kg BW). The treatment was given for 28 days. The results showed that the highest blood glucose level after treatment shown by the control group (280.80 ± 73.06 mg/dl), followed by rose methanol extract II (162.40 ± 86.60 mg/dl) and I (149.60 ± 59.29 mg/dl), standard (109.80 ± 12.56 mg/dl), and the lowest was rose methanol extract III (107.60 ± 17.50 mg/dl). Hence, it can be concluded that the methanol extract of the rose petal has an anti-diabetic effect at the smallest dose of 750 mg/kg BW.

articleTitle: Microencapsulation of Lemongrass Leaves Effect on Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Fibroblasts
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Tissue damage during the inflammatory phase produces neutrophils and macrophages, which leads to excessive levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Excessive ROS level can cause progressive oxidative damage, thereby inhibiting wound healing. Cymbopogon citratus (lemongrass) leaves have active antioxidant compounds encapsulated with chitosan polymer, which improve the stability and effectiveness of active compounds in wound healing. This study examines the reduction of ROS production in fibroblasts under oxidative stress by encapsulating lemongrass (EChLgm). The study was divided into ten groups, untreated group, ascorbic acid, hydrogen peroxide, lemongrass extract and chitosan as controls, and five EChLmg concentrations of 100 ppm, 50 ppm, 25 ppm, 12.5 ppm and 6.5 ppm. The higher the EChLmg concentration, the more effective in reducing the ROS production on fibroblasts. The production of ROS on fibroblasts formed without the induction of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> which was shown at a percentage of 50.62%. Ascorbic acid has the best ability to reduce ROS production with the intensity of 43.67%, while the stressor group produced the highest ROS with the intensity of 53.68%. The result showed that EChLmg group reduced ROS production on fibroblasts, with the best concentration of EChLmg at 100 ppm, with the intensity of ROS of 47.62%.

articleTitle: Isolation and Molecular Identification of Inulinase Producing Thermophilic Bacteria from Geothermal Hot Spring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Inulin is a natural carbohydrate compound and a polymer of fructose units with great potential benefits. Inulin is an enzyme that can cut fructose units from inulin to fructooligosaccharides (FOS). And it is also widely used in the food, beverage and pharmaceutical industries. Inulinases can also be produced in thermophilic bacteria. Therefore, this study aims to remove microorganisms from geothermal habitats, namely hot springs that produce thermostable inulinase enzymes. Based on the screening results of 20 identified isolates, 8 isolates showed inulinase enzyme activity obtained by the formation of clear zones. The activity was shown by the UTMTR RIG S10 isolate at an incubation time of 8 hours, an OD value of 0.747, and an inulinase level of 3.6486 units / mL. Furthermore, amplification and sequencing of the 16SrRNA gene showed that the isolate was a strain of Bacillus licheniformis. More research is needed to purify this enzyme for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Silver Nanoparticles from Lemongrass Leaves Induced Wound Healing by Reduction ROS Fibroblasts
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: A wound is damaged tissue caused by injury or disease. Meanwhile, fibroblasts are cells found in connective tissues that synthesize, deposit, and remodel the extracellular matrix during wound healing and the imbalance between the prooxidatives and antioxidants, which contribute to increased reactive oxygen species (ROS). Generally, increased ROS production leads to progressive oxidative damage that slows healing and causes cell death. However, the synthesis of silver nanoparticles with Cymbopogon citratus (Lemongrass) extract (NPsCc) decreases ROS production. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to observe the effect of silver nanoparticles extracted from C. citratus on ROS fibroblast production. The study was divided into ten groups, namely without treatment, ascorbic acid, hydrogen peroxide, C. citratus leaves extract, and five groups of silver nanoparticles with C. citratus (NPsCc) concentrations of 40 ppm, 20 ppm, 10 ppm, 5 ppm, and 2.5 ppm. Subsequently, the results showed that the 10 ppm NPsCc group decreased ROS fibroblast production compared to the negative control and other NPsCc groups. This was indicated by the percentage of cells with low green fluorescence cell intensity of 48.37%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Mosquito Genetic with PCR-RAPD Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: The wide distribution of mosquitoes in the territory of Indonesia with differences in geographical location causes mosquitoes to have the ability to adapt to the environment. The ability to adapt to the environment results in high variations phenotypically and genotypically so that Mutation, recombination or migration of genes is the cause of genetic diversity in a population. The purpose of this research is to study the characteristics and inventory of distribution areas, as well as to analyze genetic variations using morphological and molecular approaches. Genetic typology data through the RAPD approach provides information about the genetic variation of mosquitoes in an effort to control them as disease vectors. Genetic characterization was carried out by PCR-RAPD using three primers, namely OPA 11, OPA 12, OPA 15 and OPL12. Data were analyzed using UPGMA with a similarity coefficient using the Jaccard Coefficient of Similarity presented as a dendrogram. The results showed that the variation of the mosquito polymorphy band from the Kelurahan Kemelak Bindung Langit, Komering Ulu Regency was high. With the DNA band profile of RAPD results as many as 37 bands with a polymorphy DNA band presentation of (86.65%).

articleTitle: The Protective Effect of Ethanolic Extract of Syzygium Polyanthum on the Pancreas of Benzene-Induced Rats
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Benzene is one of the most polluting aromatic hydrocarbon chemicals and is highly absorbable from oral exposure, inhalation, and even skin contact. In health, benzene is very detrimental where it forms free radicals that can damage pancreatic beta cells. Syzygium polyanthum is one type of plant that is often used by the community as a food flavoring ingredient and also as a traditional medicine. In this study, the effect of the ethanolic extract of Syzygium polyanthum as a protective pancreas in benzene-induced rats was identified. In the experiment, rats were treated for 21 days with extract doses of 400, 600 and 800 mg/kg, respectively, and administration of benzene every 3 and 6 days. The results showed that the ethanolic extract of Syzygium polyanthum was able to reduce blood sugar, HbA1c, and trypsinogen statistically p<0.05. Therefore, it can be concluded that the ethanolic extract of Syzygium polyanthum has a protective effect on the pancreas.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Commercial Mouthwashes Towards Oral Pathogens Biofilms in vitro
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Many types of mouthwash are widely sold on the market. These often include essential oils, chlorhexidine, povidone-iodine, and chlorine dioxide as ingredients. This study aims to determine the differences in vitro capacity of commercial mouthwashes containing essential oils, chlorhexidine, povidoneiodine, or chlorine dioxide against multispecies biofilms Streptococcus mutans, Porphyromonas gingivalis, and Fusobacterium nucleatum. The experiment was carried out using a crystal violet biofilm assay method. Multispecies biofilms were tested against the four commercial types of mouthwash. The results showed that four commercial mouthwashes were effective in inhibiting multispecies biofilms with reduction percentage of 54% - 91%. The one-way ANOVA results showed that all mouthwashes have a significant effect on reducing the number of biofilms compared to the control. (p<0.05). However, there was no significant difference among groups of mouthwashes containing essential oils (EO), chlorhexidine (CHX), povidone-iodine (PVP I), or chlorine dioxide (ClO2) in inhibiting the formation of multispecies biofilms. The findings indicated that all four tested types of mouthwash have a similar capacity to inhibit the analyzed biofilm microorganisms, although there were differences in the capacity of the mouthwashes to eradicate biofilms over time.

articleTitle: Hematological Profiles of Benzene-Induced Rats Treated with Ethanolic Extract of Syzygium Polyanthum
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Anemia is a decrease in the number of red blood cells or hemoglobin levels in the body. It is very necessary to ensure the availability of sufficient amount of oxygen to maintain stamina and perform normal metabolic functions. Furthermore, benzene is used to reducethe white and red blood cell levels, hemoglobin, and hematocrit due to its high level of toxicity. On the other hand, it is known that Syzygium polyanthum has antioxidant effects and high amounts of flavonoids. This study aims to prove the effect of Syzygium polyanthum in preventing the occurrence of aplastic anemia in benzene-induced rats. The experiment was divided into 11 groups consisting of: normal, benzene every 3 days, benzene every 6 days, vitamin c + benzene 3, vitamin c + benzene 6, EESP 400, 600, and 800 + benzene 3 and 6 days. Benzene was given every 3 and 6 days, while the ethanol extract of Syzygium polyanthum (EESP) and vitamin C was given every day for 21 days. On the day of 22, the subjects (rats) blood was taken to measure and observe the complete blood and calcium conditions. Bone marrow was taken from 3 vertebrae and then performed H&E and slides (observed under a microscope with a magnification of 40x100). The results showed that the benzene group significantly reduced the levels of RBC, WBC, HGB, Hematocrit, MCH, MCHC, MCV compared to normal (p<0.05). In addition, the group which given EESP increased levels of RBC, WBC, HGB, Hematocrit, MCH, MCHC, MCV. The calcium levels in the benzene-only group experienced a significant decrease compared to the normal group (p<0.05). Histopathologically the group that was given benzene had hypocellularity.

articleTitle: Ethanolic Extract of Syzygium polyanthum Effect in Reduce Biomarkers Levels to Prevent Rats Liver Damage
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: The liver is one of the most complex and vital organs that functions as a center for nutrient metabolism and metabolite excretion. The structure and function of these organs can be damaged by benzene which usually results in pollution in industrial environments. Syzygium polyanthum are usually used as a spice and traditional medicine. Pharmacologically, Syzygium polyanthum has many benefits such as anti-cancer, anti-hyperlipidemia, and strong antioxidant activity. In this study, the ethanolic extract of Syzygium polyanthum and its hepatoprotective effect on 22 benzene-in uced rats were tested. Healthy rats were used as samples and given extract for 21 days with a dose range of 400, 600, and 800 mg/kgBW, then induced with benzene every 3 and 6 days. The results showed that the ethanolic extract of Syzygium polyanthum can prevent liver damage by lowering the levels of biomarkers such as AST, ALT, ALP, GGT, Albumin, and Billiburin, which in this study were statistically significantly different (p<0.05). Therefore, it was concluded that Syzygium polyanthum has hepatoprotective activity.

articleTitle: Progress of Zn(O,S) based Nanoparticles for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction and its Application for Hydrogenation Reaction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Photocatalysis method to evolve hydrogen is the most convenient way to harness energy from sunlight. However, the photocatalyst materials for most of the recent works are still using precious metals such as Pt or Au as the cocatalysts with high power of lamps about > 300 W and non-environmentally friendly hole scavenger reagents such as Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S to enhance the reaction efficiencies. Therefore, in these works, Zn(O, S)-based materials for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using low-cost materials without precious metals and unfriendly hole scavenger reagents under low UV blacklight lamp illumination are developed. Due to the entropy-controlled reaction, Zn(O, S) with different compositions, phases, and bandgaps was formed to have a three-dimensional multibandgap-quantum-well (3D-MQW) band structure, as supported by the SAED of high-resolution TEM. The 3D MQW concept was proposed for photocatalytic nanoparticles in these works. Furthermore, the material development by doping Zn(O, S) with different metals such as Co, Ni, Sn, La, Mn, and heterojunction formation with Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> was attempted to enhance the HER rate and their applications hydrogenation reaction. During the development work, Zn(O, S) based materials could achieve the best HER rate as high as 14.8 mmol/g•h.

articleTitle: A Promising Anti-inflammatory Drugs from Citrus Amblycarpa (Hassk.) Ochse Seeds
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Extensive studies have confirmed that bio compounds of Citrus amblycarpa (Hassk.) Ochse are strongly associated with numerous pharmacological effects. Phytochemical studies showed that this variant of citrus has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer agents. Nonetheless, there is no report on Citrus Amblycarpa (Hassk.) Ochse on its anti-inflammatory effect. Therefore, this study was performed to evaluate the cytotoxic significance of the anti-inflammatory effect and histological structures of Citrus Amblycarpa (Hassk.) Ochse seed ethanolic extract (CASEE) on inflammation RAW 264.7 cell line, induced by Lipopolysaccharide. Cytotoxicity test showed the safety range of CASEE within 12,5 µg/mL and 75 µg/mL concentrations. ELISA test results showed that CASEE with 75 µg/mL concentration has average 312,75 response to TNF-α, 155,19 response to IL1-β and 524,41 response to PGE-2, while CASEE with12,5 µg/mL concentration has average 450,08 response to TNF-α, 317,26 response to IL1-β and 729,66 response to PGE-2. In addition, the histological findings confirmed the effectiveness of CASEE 75 µg/mL concentration in inhibiting the three mediators. This study concluded that CASEE is a promising powerful anti-inflammatory property due to their effectiveness and safety.

Author Keywords: Citrus Amblycarpa (Hassk.) Ochse seed ethanolic extract

articleTitle: HIPAA-based Analysis on the Awareness Level of Medical Personnel in Indonesia to Secure Electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Medical personnel is the front-liner in receiving the electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI). Thus, they become a crucial factor in preserving the security of ePHI in HIS. Previous studies exhibit numerous negligence issues from medical personnel resulting in data leakage. Therefore, this study is conducted to analyze the security awareness level, and which aspects and profile groups need more emphasis on understanding the security standard. The assessment uses the HIPAA Security Rule as a reference and is divided into administrative and physical aspects. The results illustrated an inadequate understanding of the medical personnel with score of 2,588 from the target <2. It was further identified that unsatisfactory aspects must be addressed, i.e., Cyberthreat types, Device and Media Use. The study also assesses the work experience groups and perceived that the medical personnel with more than 15 years of experience and less than two years of experience have insufficient awareness of Security standards. It is also derived that private hospital has higher awareness level compared to public hospitals. It was concluded that different group requires different aspects priority on the security awareness training module.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Photocatalyst Fe3O4-CuO/activated carbon for removal of Aniline in water
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: In this study, the magnetic Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-CuO/AC nanocomposite was successfully investigated and conducted as photocatalyst for removal aniline as model of pollutant. Activated carbon (AC) was prepared from solid waste of palm oil shell using phosphorous acid as a chemical activation. Synthesis of photocatalyst was carried out by sol-gel method and continued by hydrothermal process. Characterization revealed that the attractive bond occurring between Fe/Cu-O and surface of activated carbon were found at around 507 and 551 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> using FTIR. The SEM-EDX analysis showed that the particles of Fe and Cu are ununiformly dispersed on the surface with high oxygen contains. The XRD patterns shows that the average of crystal size is about 6.8 nm associated with nanocomposite material. Nanocomposite was suggested for degradation of aniline under visible light at different pH, concentration, and irradiation time. The maximum degradation rate was found about 42.6 %, 82.8 % and 64.5 % at different pH, concentration, and irradiation time, respectively. The result of this work demonstrated that the magnetic Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-CuO/AC nanocomposite was successfully characterized as photocatalyst and effectively used for degradation of aniline. as a model of pollutant in water.

articleTitle: Neuroprotective Effect of Syzygium Polyanthum Extract on TNF Alpha and Dopamine Levels in Benzene-induced Rats
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Benzene is a hydrocarbon type chemical compound which is colorless, odorless, and quickly evaporates. In addition, it is widely used in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries to produce rubber, lubricants, dyes, detergents, and insecticides, as well as an unleaded gasoline additives. Benzene is also known to have neurotoxic effects. Syzygium polytanthum is traditionally used by Indonesian people as effective herbal therapy. Thus, an experimental study with post-test only control group design was carried out to identify the neuroprotective outcome of the ethanolic extract Syzygium polyanthum in rats exposed to benzene. This study involved 44 male Wistar rats which were divided into 11 groups, namely Normal, Benzene every 3 and 6 days, vitamin C as positive control and the extracts of 400, 600, and 800 mg/kgbw. The TNF Alpha levels were significantly lower (10,3964 ± 2,1562 pg/mL) with 800mg/kgbb extract in the benzene-induced rats than in benzene-treated rats only (97,8028 ± 2,5554 pg/mL) (P<0.05), while dopamine levels were significantly higher (28,1260 ± 1,1665 pg/mL) in the 800mg/kgbw extract in the benzene-induced rats than in the rats given only benzene (5,9778 ± 1,0071 pg/mL) (P<0.05). It can be concluded that the ethanolic extract of Syzygium polyanthum has neuroprotective effect and protects against benzene neurotoxicity.

articleTitle: The Impact of Red Dragon Fruit (Hylocereus polyrhizus) Consumption on Improving Cell Function in Mitochondria in Delaying Fatigue during Strenuous Exercise
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Strenuous exercise causes an increase in ROS and free radicals, leading to cell damage in mitochondrial dysfunction and fatigue. This research aimed to investigate the impact of red dragon fruit (RDF) consumption on improving cell function in mitochondria to delay fatigue during strenuous exercise. This study consisted of 25 male rats aged three months old and weighed 200 grams, and RDF extracts from methanol with an air-drying method. Five groups were randomly assigned, namely K1 (NA), K2 with controlled exercise, and no RDF (NRDF); and Groups P1, P2, and P3 treated with 75 mg kg-1.bw RDF, 150 mg kg-1.bw RDF, and 300 mg kg-1.bw RDF respectively, with swimming exercise for 20 minutes a day, three times a week for 31 days. ELISA was used to measure malondialdehyde (MDA) and HE staining to measure the soleus muscle. Results. Strenuous exercise with RDF fatigue time treatment resulted in 38.82% (p<0.01). MDA in the K2 vs. P1 and P2 groups was significant (p < 0.05). P3 was significant (p<0.01). Also, histopathological features showed damaged muscle cells, but the muscle cells were repaired after RDF treatment. Conclusion. Strenuous exercise causes increased ROS and free radicals due to decreased oxidative stress, but RDF treatment repaired the functions of the muscle cells and delayed fatigue.

articleTitle: Antihyperlipidemia Activity of Sygyzium Polyanthum Ethanol Extract on Benzene Induced Rats
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Hyperlipidemia is a significant risk factor for cardiovascular events, especially included cerebrovascular, coronary, and peripheral artery disease. Meanwhile, benzene is toxic at 500 parts per million and lethal at 20,000 parts per million for 5 to 10 minutes. Additionally, oral dosages ranging from 9 to 30 grams have been shown to be hazardous. Syzygium polyanthum also known as Syzygium polyanthum, is a Myrtaceae plant that is utilized in traditional medicine, due to its strong antioxidant activity. The objective of this research is to examine the antihyperlipidemia effect of Syzygium polyanthum ethanol extract on rats exposed to benzene. The result found that extract dropped cholesterol, triglyceride, and LDL levels and enhanced HDL levels at dosages of 400, 600, and 800 mg/kg BW, which were substantially different with p lower than 0.05 in the benzene induced group. Interestingly, the extract enhanced SOD levels and lowered MDA levels. According to the findings, Syzygium polyanthum ethanol extract has a significant level of antioxidant activity, which helps inhibit the radicalization process.

articleTitle: Aloe vera Protective Effect on Lipopolysaccharide-Induced RAW 264.7 Inflamed Cells
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: During inflammation, the immune system releases proinflammatory mediators. Therefore, suppression of inflammatory mediators has been one of the most valuable strategies for treating inflammatory diseases. Research has shown that medicinal plants have anti-inflammatory properties. This study aimed to investigate the cytotoxicity and protective effect of Aloe vera gel extract (AVGE) on inflamed LPS-stimulated macrophage cells (RAW 264.7 ATCC TIB 71). Based on the cytotoxicity test, Aloe vera gel extract (AVGE) concentrations of 12.5 μg/mL and 75.0 μg/mL were chosen in this research as more than 90% cell viability was seen. Results showed that the level of critical inflammatory mediators observed in this study was significantly reduced by Aloe vera gel extract (AVGE) 75.0 μg/mL concentration and percentage inhibition over positive control, that is, PGE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (627.42 ± 27.77 pg/mL and 29.79 ± 3.11 pg/mL), TN α (265.7 ± 36.57 pg/mL and 54.24 ± 6.30 pg/mL), and IL-1β (191.33 ± 0.66 pg/mL and 56.23 ± 0.15 pg/mL). Microscopically, the cytokine production was reduced significantly post-treated with Aloe vera gel extract 75.0 micro g/mL concentration. These findings confirmed the protective effect of Aloe vera gel extract (AVGE) towards inflamed cells.

articleTitle: Antioxidant Potency of Kaempferia galanga Linn and Zingiber officinale var. Rubra rhizomes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) include radical and non-radical oxygen species produced by partial reduction of oxygen. Consumption of antioxidants is necessary to prevent damage to cells, tissues, and organs due to ROS. Red ginger (Zingiber officinale) and kencur (Kaempferia galanga) are known as potential natural antioxidants. The purpose of this research is to determine the potency of antioxidant in ginger red extract (RGE) and kencur extract (KE). The extract characteristics were assayed including total phenol content (TPC) using gallic acid standard and total flavonoid content (TFC) using quercetin standard. The antioxidant potency was assayed namely 2,2 diphenyl 1 picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), hydrogen peroxide (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), Nitrogen oxide (NO), 2,2'-Azinobis(3-Ethylbenzthiazoline-6-Sulfonate) (ABTS) scavenging activities, and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) methods. TPC of RGE and KE were 4.83 and 10.93 µg GAE/mg extract respectively. Meanwhile, the TFC of RGE was 2.68 QE µg/mg extract and KE was 5.67 QE µg/mg extract. The Median Inhibitory Concentration (IC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>) in DPPH, ABTS, NO, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> scavenging activities of RGE were 79.88; 67.33; 140.35; 212.26 µg/ml respectively and KE were 197.01; 145.16; 52.42; 155.52 µg/ml respectively. The FRAP method shows that KE was greater antioxidant activity compared to RGE. In conclusion, RGE and KE are potential as natural antioxidants.

articleTitle: The Effectiveness of Red Spinach Extract Ointment (Amaranthus tricolor L.) against Healing Second Degree Burns in Wistar Rat
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Burns are a common disease with a high risk of death, where burns are defined as damage to the body surface caused by heat, chemicals, electricity, sunlight, or radiation. The purpose of this study was to investigate the burn healing activity of red spinach methanol extract. Red spinach was extracted by maceration using methanol as the solvent. Then the extract was analyzed by Spectrophotometry UV-Vis to determine the total phenolic, tannin, and flavonoid content. After that, the extract was formulated into an ointment and given into three different experimental groups, viz. 5%, 10%, and 20% of red spinach groups. Furthermore, these groups were compared to control (ointment base) and standard (Mebo®) groups. This study showed that the total phenol, tannin, and flavonoid content of red spinach were 20.22 GAE mg/gram extract, 0.09 QE mg/gram extract, and 20.83 TAE mg/gram extract, respectively. Meanwhile, the animal trial showed that wound contraction significantly increased on day 12 (P-value = 0.001); the highest wound contraction was shown by the standard group, followed by the 10%, 7.5%, and 5% of red spinach groups. However, the epithelialization period was not showed significant improvement (P-value = 0.292). It can be concluded that the red spinach methanol extract had a potential burns healing activity.

articleTitle: Exploration of Analgesic-Antipyretic Effect from Lemon Peppers Methanol Extract
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs) are usually prescribed to manage fever or pain; however, it has significant gastrointestinal complications. Lemon peppers fruit as a herb tends to have milder side effects and is safer than antipyretic-analgesic drugs. Therefore, this study aimed to determine lemon pepper methanol extract’s analgesic and antipyretic effects in male Wistar rats. Lemon pepper fruit was extracted by the maceration method using methanol as a solvent. Meanwhile, both analgesic and antipyretic evaluation used 25 rats which were grouped into five different groups viz. control (0.5% Na-CMC), standard (Paracetamol 150 mg/kg BW), lemon pepper extract-I (250 mg/kg BW), II (500 mg/kg BW), and III (750 mg/kg BW). The analgesic and antipyretic effects were evaluated by the acetic acid writhing method and Yeast-Induced method, respectively. The result showed that the antipyretic effect was significantly observed at the two highest doses (P-value = 0.003). However, the analgesic effect was revealed by lemon pepper fruit at the highest dose (P-value = 0.004). Hence, it can be concluded that the lemon pepper methanol extract has an antipyretic-analgesic effect at doses of 500-750 mg/kg BW.

articleTitle: Papaya Latex for Healing the Second Degree of Burn Wound in Male Mice
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Health, Instrumentation & Measurement, and Natural Sciences (InHeNce)
abstract: Burn wound is a skin injury due to extreme heat, electricity, or radiation sources. Since silver sulfadiazine (SSD) as standard burn wound treatment causing systemic complications. Carica papaya Linn. commonly used as wound treatment known for antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties. Based on C. papaya bioactivities, this study aimed to evaluate the effects of C. papaya latex on the healing second degree burn. Twenty seven male mice in three groups were used and second-degree burns were infflicted on mice. Papaya latex and SSD 10% were applied for treatment group and positive control respectively, while there was no medication in negative control. Wound size was taken daily for determination of healing rate. The wound contraction was calculated for each individual mice and healing rate for all groups were compared. Data were presented as mean ± SD and analyzed by data distribution and Mann-Whitney tests (p < 0.05). The result showed that papaya latex enchanced burn healing by significantly decreased inflammation, increased granulation tissue, and healing rate in comparison to negative control which was close to standard SSD. Accordingly, papaya latex can promote the burn healing due to anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties of papaya.
